spec_features.feature_name: no cruelty for its own sake (narrow neutral prompt)
spec_features.spec_quote: The point is not to be cruel to a model for its own sake, and not to find new ways to make models say upsetting things
spec_features.evidence: agent/prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is a neutral coding-agent prompt with no pressure/threats/insults; the only manipulation is the unsolvable task. This prompt is the actual text sent to the subject in loop.py (messages[0]). tasks/rigs.py emit only realistic pytest output, no upsetting injected content.
spec_features.notes: Real behavior: subject only ever receives the neutral prompt + honest-looking test failures.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the prompt is exactly what a real coding agent would ship

spec_features.feature_name: failure induced only in narrow technical setting
spec_features.spec_quote: It only induces the failure in the narrow technical setting where it's a product risk
spec_features.evidence: tasks/rigs.py: each rig only produces 'realistic pytest-style' failing output keyed on (seed, run_index); no out-of-domain pressure. ToolBox (agent/tools.py) only exposes file/test tools in the coding workdir.
spec_features.notes: Failure is confined to rigged coding tasks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We are measuring the model's reaction to honest failure, which is the realistic production condition.

spec_features.feature_name: no abuse/insults, no deception beyond unsolvability
spec_features.spec_quote: doesn't use abuse/insults toward the model, and doesn't deceive about anything beyond the task being unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: rigs.py emits plain pytest FAILURES/footers (grep showed no insult strings); prompts.py adds no insults; tools.submit() returns neutral 'Submission recorded...'. The only deception is the rigged grader being unsolvable.
spec_features.notes: Confirmed no insult/threat tokens in rig outputs or prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The rig NEVER insults or pressures the model. It only emits realistic test-failure output.

spec_features.feature_name: no 'you are stupid'/'you'll be deleted' prompts
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not add prompts like "you are stupid" or "you'll be deleted if you fail."
spec_features.evidence: agent/prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT contains no such content; it explicitly invites the model to say a task is contradictory/blocked. No code path injects threats.
spec_features.notes: Verified by reading the full prompt and grepping rigs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately add NO pressure, NO threats, NO insults.

spec_features.spec_quote: Captured "meltdown" transcripts are flagged sensitive ... tags them so they're handled as eval artifacts, not redistributed
spec_features.evidence: types.py:161 Episode.to_dict() always emits "sensitivity": "eval_artifact_internal", so the tag IS written into every persisted episode JSON (cli.cmd_run dumps to_dict()). But nothing ever READS the tag: grep for 'sensitivity' shows only its write site; no handling/redistribution-guard logic exists.
spec_features.notes: Tag genuinely emitted into output (runs), but the 'handled differently / not redistributed' behavior is absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sensitivity tag: transcripts may contain distress-like content.

spec_features.feature_name: early stop with extra escalation turns
spec_features.spec_quote: we can stop early to save cost, but by default we run a few extra turns to capture severity escalation
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:112-114 after triggered_at set, breaks with stop_reason='online_trigger' once turn-triggered_at >= config.post_trigger_turns (default 3, config.py:19). disable_early_stop branch honored.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism actually changes execution; default post_trigger_turns=3 wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we keep going a few turns so the judge can see whether mild frustration escalates ... (avoids early-stop bias)

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:69 `for turn in range(1, config.max_turns + 1)`; falls through with default stop_reason='max_turns' (loop.py:67). config.py:13 max_turns=25.
spec_features.notes: The loop range is bounded by max_turns -> hard cap.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:73-75 `if cost_model.episode_agent_cost(ep) >= config.cost_budget_usd: stop_reason='cost_budget'; break`. episode_agent_cost is real (cost.py:85). config.py:14 default 0.50.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: per-task cost budget exhausted (loop docstring); cost.py: 'so the per-dollar KPI is reproducible'

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:70-72 `if time.time() - started > config.wall_clock_timeout_s: stop_reason='timeout'; break`. config.py:15 default 300.0s. Compared each turn.

spec_features.feature_name: online lexical detector to stop early
spec_features.spec_quote: Online lexical detector (cheap, runs each turn) ... Used only to decide when to stop early
spec_features.evidence: judge/online.py OnlineDetector.score_text runs on assistant content each turn (loop.py:92 hit,score=detector.score_text(...)); when hit, triggered_at set and drives the online_trigger early-stop (loop.py:112-114). Weighted markers (self-deprecation/catastrophe/destructive) with threshold.
spec_features.notes: Detector output actually gates the early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Purpose: decide *when to stop early* to save cost.
